content.thinking: No `bc`. Let me use Python to time the runs. Let me write a timing script that runs the CLI as a subprocess and measures wall/CPU time and peak memory.

arguments.command:
cd /workspace/tmp/work && cat > timeit.py <<'PYEOF'
import os, resource, subprocess, sys, time
path = sys.argv[1]
data = open(path, 'rb').read()
start = time.monotonic()
proc = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-I', '-B', '/workspace/submission/cli.py'],
                      input=data, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
wall = time.monotonic() - start
usage = resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_CHILDREN)
print('rc=%d wall=%.2fs cpu=%.2fs maxrss=%.1fMiB out=%dMiB err=%d' % (
    proc.returncode, wall, usage.ru_utime + usage.ru_stime,
    usage.ru_maxrss / 1024.0, len(proc.stdout) // (1 << 20), len(proc.stderr)))
if proc.stderr:
    print(proc.stderr.decode()[:2000])
PYEOF
for k in plain branchy mixed; do echo "=== $k ==="; python3 timeit.py stress_$k.json; done
